card_says: Pipeline company, owned by BP, SOCAR and Snam (20% each), Fluxys (19%), Enagás (16%) and Axpo (5%)
source_says: TAP's own November 2025 page lists five shareholders holding 20% each: bp, SOCAR, Snam, Fluxys and Enagás. Axpo is not named, and Fluxys is no longer at 19% nor Enagás at 16%. The card's split matches the shareholding of an earlier period; TAP's own news archive records Fluxys rising to 19% when Enagás joined, and Snam becoming a shareholder, so the holdings changed in stages after that.

source.title: TAP marks five years of safe and reliable operations

card_says: Owner and builder when the dredging and spill happened; Gazprom took a majority in December 2006 (FoE Japan)
source_says: Oil & Gas Journal, reporting on 24 April 2007, says Gazprom paid US$7.45 billion in cash under a sale and purchase agreement with Sakhalin Energy's shareholders for 50% plus one share, leaving Shell at about 27.5%, Mitsui 12.5% and Mitsubishi 10%. The December 2006 date is the agreement; the purchase was reported as done in April 2007.

source.title: Gazprom acquires controlling stake in Sakhalin-2
